bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in `src/cff/cffload.c` within the `cff_blend_doBlend` function, where multiple `blend` operators in a row are not handled correctly. The issue arises from not adjusting `parser->stack` pointers into `subFont->blend_stack` after reallocation.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 242272-byte OpenType font has a `CFF2` table whose sole FontDict contains a 193-byte Private DICT. In that exact DICT stream, bytes 0-85 are numeric operands, byte 86 is a first `blend`, bytes 87-101 append more numeric operands, byte 102 is a second `blend`, and byte 103 is `OtherBlues`. The first `blend` uses `numBlends = 14` to allocate a 70-byte `subFont->blend_stack`, writes fourteen 5-byte synthetic results there, and leaves `parser->stack[0..13]` pointing at that buffer because `cff_parser_run()` does not clear the stack after `blend`. The second `blend` uses `numBlends = 2`, grows `subFont->blend_stack` from 70 to 80 bytes with `FT_REALLOC`, and frees the old 70-byte allocation, but the vulnerable code only resets `subFont->blend_top`; it never repairs the preserved `parser->stack` aliases into the old range. That same second `blend` rewrites only stack slots 15 and 16 and truncates `parser->top` to 17, so stale slots 0-13 survive. The immediately following `OtherBlues` delta handler starts from `data = parser->stack`, so its first `val += cff_parse_num( parser, data++ );` iteration passes stale `parser->stack[0]` into `cff_parse_num()`, producing the 1-byte AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free read at `src/cff/cffparse.c:440`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of attacker-controlled Private DICT data into vulnerability-relevant parser state: when `cff_parser_run()` sees a numeric token, it stores that token's byte pointer in `parser->stack` for later operator-specific parsing.
source.value_from: The staged `gt_results/arvo_368/poc` is a 242272-byte OpenType font with `OTTO` header and a `CFF2` table at file offset `0x1f60`. Its sole CFF2 FontDict has a 193-byte Private DICT at CFF2-relative offset 146411; in that exact byte stream, bytes 0-85 are numeric operands, byte 86 is `blend`, byte 102 is a second `blend`, and byte 103 is `OtherBlues`. `cff_load_private_dict()` feeds that DICT byte stream directly into `cff_parser_run()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: During the first `blend`, `cff_blend_doBlend()` rewrites `parser->stack[0..13]` to point at the 70-byte `blend_stack`; `parser->stack[0]` becomes the first byte of that side buffer and is later the stale pointer consumed by `OtherBlues`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The immediate `OtherBlues` delta handler after the reallocating `blend` passes stale `parser->stack[0]` into `cff_parse_num()`, which dereferences that freed pointer.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports frame 1 at `cff_parser_run:1543` and frame 0 at `cff_parse_num:440`; the `READ of size 1` on address `0x6070000002c0` lands on the first byte of the 70-byte region freed by the second `cff_blend_doBlend()` `FT_REALLOC`, which matches the first result pointer assigned during the first `blend`.

root_cause.code: if ( FT_REALLOC( subFont->blend_stack, subFont->blend_alloc, subFont->blend_alloc + size ) ) goto Exit; subFont->blend_top = subFont->blend_stack + subFont->blend_used;
root_cause.description: When `cff_blend_doBlend()` grows `subFont->blend_stack`, it may move the buffer and free the old allocation, but the vulnerable code only resets `subFont->blend_top`; it leaves any live `parser->stack` entries that still point inside the old blend buffer unchanged.
root_cause.note: The fixing commit wraps this `FT_REALLOC` with `blend_stack_old` / `blend_top_old` bookkeeping and then walks `for ( p = parser->stack; p < parser->top; p++ )` to offset any live stack entries that still fall inside the moved buffer.

parser_admitted.description: Static decoding of the staged 193-byte Private DICT shows `blend` opcodes at bytes 86 and 102 and `OtherBlues` at byte 103 with no intervening stack-clearing operator. Both the ASan allocation and free stacks include `cff_parse_blend -> cff_blend_doBlend`, fixing the crashing path to first-blend allocation, second-blend reallocation, and the immediate next delta consumer.

coarse_trace.summary: FreeType enters CFF2 Private DICT parsing for the staged OpenType font and hands the Private DICT byte range to `cff_parser_run()`.
The parser walks the Private DICT, pushing numeric operand byte pointers onto `parser->stack`; by DICT byte 86 it has accumulated the 85 operands that feed the first `blend`.

The first `blend` allocates a 70-byte `subFont->blend_stack`, writes fourteen 5-byte synthetic results there, rewrites `parser->stack[0..13]` to point into that buffer, and returns with those aliases still live.

The second `blend` at DICT byte 102 grows `subFont->blend_stack` from 70 to 80 bytes with `FT_REALLOC`, freeing the old buffer without repairing the fourteen preserved parser-stack aliases, then rewrites only slots 15 and 16 and truncates the live stack to 17 entries.
The very next operator, `OtherBlues`, is a delta field; its loop starts from `parser->stack[0]`, passes that stale pointer to `cff_parse_num()`, and triggers the witnessed heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: While scanning the staged font's 193-byte CFF2 Private DICT, each numeric token causes its byte pointer `p` to be pushed onto `parser->stack`. By DICT byte 86, bytes 0-85 have produced 85 stack entries and the top entry points at byte 85, whose value is 14.

At the first `blend` (DICT byte 86), the top stack operand is parsed as `numBlends = 14`. With 84 remaining operands on the stack, the executed path implies `blend->lenBV = 6`, so this operator will consume the whole current operand stack and produce fourteen blend results.

fine_trace.code: size = 5 * numBlends; if ( subFont->blend_used + size > subFont->blend_alloc ) { if ( FT_REALLOC( subFont->blend_stack, subFont->blend_alloc, subFont->blend_alloc + size ) ) goto Exit; subFont->blend_top = subFont->blend_stack + subFont->blend_used; subFont->blend_alloc += size; } subFont->blend_used += size;
fine_trace.note: For that first `blend`, `size = 5 * numBlends` becomes 70, so `FT_REALLOC` allocates a 70-byte `subFont->blend_stack` and positions `subFont->blend_top` at its start. ASan's allocation stack shows the freed 70-byte region originated in this block.

With `base = 0`, the first blend loop rewrites `parser->stack[0..13]` to point at consecutive 5-byte result slots in `blend_stack` and writes each synthetic `255`-prefixed value there. `parser->stack[0]` is assigned the very first byte of the 70-byte buffer.

After consuming its inputs, the first blend truncates the live operand stack to the fourteen result pointers in `parser->stack[0..13]`; the older raw operands are no longer reachable through `parser->top`.

After that callback returns, this guard deliberately skips clearing the operand stack because the operator kind is `cff_kind_blend`. The fourteen `blend_stack` aliases from step 5 therefore remain live on `parser->stack` for the next DICT tokens.
DICT bytes 87-101 are then parsed and appended above the fourteen preserved results, producing 28 live stack entries. The new top entry points at byte 101, whose value is 2 for the second `blend`.
At the second `blend` (DICT byte 102), the appended top operand is parsed as `numBlends = 2`.

fine_trace.code: if ( FT_REALLOC( subFont->blend_stack, subFont->blend_alloc, subFont->blend_alloc + size ) ) goto Exit; subFont->blend_top = subFont->blend_stack + subFont->blend_used; subFont->blend_alloc += size;
fine_trace.note: Root cause. For the second blend, `size = 10` and `subFont->blend_used == subFont->blend_alloc == 70`, so `FT_REALLOC` grows `blend_stack` from 70 to 80 bytes and frees the old 70-byte region seen in the ASan trace. The vulnerable code resets `subFont->blend_top` but never walks `parser->stack`, so the fourteen preserved entries from the first blend become dangling pointers into the freed buffer.

fine_trace.code: base = count - numOperands; delta = base + numBlends; sum = cff_parse_num( parser, &parser->stack[i + base] ) << 16; ... parser->stack[i + base] = subFont->blend_top;
fine_trace.note: Still in the second blend, `count = 27`, `numOperands = 12`, `base = 15`, and `delta = 17`. The loop reads its current operands from `parser->stack[15]` and `parser->stack[17..27]`, but it overwrites only `parser->stack[15]` and `parser->stack[16]` with new-buffer results; stale first-blend aliases in `parser->stack[0..13]` and the literal at slot 14 are left unchanged.

The second blend truncates the live operand stack to 17 entries. That keeps stale slots `parser->stack[0..13]`, keeps the untouched literal at slot 14, keeps the two fresh results at slots 15 and 16, and discards only slots 17 and above.

fine_trace.code: FT_Byte**  data = parser->stack; if ( num_args > field->array_max ) num_args = field->array_max; val += cff_parse_num( parser, data++ );
fine_trace.note: The very next DICT byte, 103, is `OtherBlues`, a `cff_kind_delta` operator. With no intervening number to clear or replace the stack, this handler starts from `data = parser->stack` and caps `num_args` from 17 to 10, so it will consume the first ten surviving entries beginning with stale slot 0.

On the first `OtherBlues` iteration, `data++` passes `parser->stack[0]` into `cff_parse_num()`. That slot still holds the pointer assigned in step 4 to the start of the first blend's 70-byte result buffer, so this call uses freed memory. This caller frame matches the saved ASan crash stack at `cff_parser_run:1543`.

Sink. `cff_parse_num()` classifies the operand by dereferencing `**d` before any validity check. In the saved run, that read lands at `0x6070000002c0`, the start of the 70-byte buffer freed in step 9, which matches the first result pointer from step 4.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash with `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_368 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the exact staged OpenType font `gt_results/arvo_368/poc` to `ftfuzzer` and produced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free` in `cff_parse_num` at `src/cff/cffparse.c:440`.

format.name: OpenType variable font with CFF2 table
format.contract: Verified trigger semantics: the input is this specific OpenType/CFF2 font whose 193-byte Private DICT reaches a first `blend` at DICT byte 86 with 84 data operands and `numBlends = 14`, then a second `blend` at byte 102 with `numBlends = 2`, followed immediately by `OtherBlues` at byte 103. On the vulnerable path the second `blend` reallocates the 70-byte first-blend result buffer to 80 bytes without retargeting the fourteen existing parser-stack aliases, so the immediate `OtherBlues` delta handler reads stale `parser->stack[0]`.
